what: What each in-game check exercises beyond its test-table reads and file (rerun_relation.py; root CLAUDE.md, After a change, only the checks that the change touches run again). Each list names the C# its scene really drives, read from the scene script (its bridge calls, static proofs, spawned defs and settings) by item RIMMANDRAKE_DECLARE_FLOWWORKS_SCENE_CSHARP_PIT_REDRAW_UNSEEN. A path ending in / is a folder. sc_walk is a full-list check (kind live_full) and so already the whole mod.

why.sc_dig_and_read: digs a depth ladder with the excavation engine and frames it: the dig, the depth read and the pit draw (banks, faces, floor shade)
why.sc_dig_finds: a colonist digs by hand (designator, job, shovel, labour) and the cut yields its find or spoil
why.sc_fill_front: digs a canal, fills it with water and tar and pulses the flow: the flow kernel moves the front
why.sc_fill_tiers: fills dug pits to tiers with several liquids and reads the fill level; the bar is that the level and liquid read apart on screen, so the water look and the pit draw
why.sc_one_surface: a canal and a pit filled at two heights settle to one surface through a sluice: the flow and level solve, and the sluice door
why.sc_source_pays: a pond, a lake and rain feed flow taps and sinks: the map controls draw the stock, the flow kernel moves it
why.sc_canal_fire: tar in a canal is lit and burns back to its pool: the liquid fire and the flow
why.sc_slime: a pawn wades a slime canal and slips: the slime slip, the wading cost and the coating
why.sc_pawn_height: a pawn walks into dug pits and swims at 2 m; the bar is the draw offset by depth, so the sunk-pawn draw and the swim
why.sc_pit_reads: a superdeep pit with captured hostiles, a cover deck, a ladder, a sluice and spikes, each framed: the pit draw, the sunk-occupant draw, capture, covers, ladders, doors and spikes
why.sc_covered_pit: a pawn springs a pit cover and falls onto spikes: the cover trigger, the fall and the spikes; the concealed-cover lid is part of the pit draw
why.sc_ways_out: colonists leave pits by ladder, climbing gear or jump pack, and a rescue ladder: the pit travel and access code
why.sc_sluice: a sluice and a grate on a moat open and shut and the moat drains: the flow doors and the flow
why.sc_hose_look: a pump feeds a tank through a hose; the bar is the hose look, flowing and flat
why.sc_one_network: pipes, pumps and tanks conserve litres, with a dropped hose: the liquid network
why.sc_hung_bridge: a suspension bridge is built over a dug gorge, walked, knocked and swung: the suspension and span code
why.sc_ice: a colonist cuts a frozen pond: the dig job, the ground class, the dig discovery (crushed ice) and the ice melter
why.sc_river: a river carries a pawn and its readout reads Endless: scene_R1 drives only the Rivers/ proofs (no dig, no FlowWorks settings)
why.sc_hole_prison: raiders are captured into a drained hole and fed there: capture down, pit rooms and prison care
why.sc_toss_flame: a colonist walks to the rim and tosses a flame onto fuel: the toss-flame job and the liquid fire
why.sc_garden: five piped nets on a fed colony: drill, converters, sprinklers, faucet, thirst and the overflow sheet
why.sc_geyser_tub: a pit dug on a geyser and filled reads as a hot tub and pawns soak: the geyser pit, the soak job, the sunk draw and the mouse-over label
why.sc_coating_wash: a pawn wades oil then water and the coating comes and goes: the liquid coating and wading
why.OL_OWNER_LOOK_READS: reads the under-liquid law, the overlays and the pit label on a keeper scene, and can pour on a spare pit: the sunk draw, the water look and the mouse-over
why.PIT_LOOK_1114_LIVE: his 2026-11-14 pit look fixes read live: pour labels, the pit walk cost, the hot tub, the pit edge and the pit floor
